subject: AsterHealth dedicated pool activation — sprint & regional priority agreement
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@asterhealth.com>, Platform Team <platform@asterhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: AsterHealth dedicated pool activation — sprint & regional priority agreement

Hi Elaine / AsterPlatform team,

Great to be kicking this off — thanks for the time on Friday. Per our pilot discussion, I wanted to align on an initial activation sprint and regional priorities so we can book engineering capacity and a preflight window. Attached are the SOW v2 and a compact activation checklist to make the handoff cleaner.

High-level propose: 
- Primary region: us-west1 (latency critical for west-coast clinicians)
- Secondary region: us-east1 for failover/replica capacity
- Initial capacity: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved pool) with autoscale to 20 during scheduled bursts
- Autoscale policy: 60% sustained utilization triggers + queued-request threshold; burst allowed for up to 2 hours/day during go-live week
- KV cache warmup: we'll run a short warmup job 2 hours prior to first scheduled traffic window

Next steps I need from your side: 
1) Confirm primary/secondary region preference and any hard constraints (e.g., data residency).
2) Confirm acceptable burst windows (dates/times) and SLAs for failover.
3) Any compliance asks re: audit logs / HIPAA that should be in the SOW.

Ops / Monica & Karthik — please review the proposed capacity and give a high-level feasibility + any configuration notes we should send to the AsterPlatform team. If feasible, can we aim to schedule the preflight window the week of 2027-05-17?

Thanks,
Priyom

--
Priyom Das

From: Elaine Park <elaine@asterhealth.com>

Date: 2027-05-01T12:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AsterHealth dedicated pool activation — sprint & regional priority agreement

Priyom,

Thanks — this looks good and actionable. A few clarifications from our side:
- Region: us-west1 as primary is fine. We do have an internal requirement that PHI logs remain in the US; no EU region for this deployment.
- Burst windows: Our prime clinical hours are 07:00–18:00 PT. For go-live we can accept a 2-hour burst window during 09:00–11:00 PT for the first three days to validate scale, then expand as needed.
- Compliance: we need SOC2 + HIPAA logging enabled; can you confirm retention for audit logs (minimum 180 days) and whether Redwood can stream logs to our Splunk instance (platform@redwood.ai integration)?

Also, can you share the expected RPS and concurrency assumptions you're making for the 8->20 pool sizing? That will help our infra lead validate failover behavior.

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Platform, AsterHealth
elaine@asterhealth.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: AsterHealth dedicated pool activation — sprint & regional priority agreement

Monica / Karthik — forwarding Elaine's notes. Two urgent asks from customer: 1) confirm log retention (180 days) + Splunk streaming; 2) provide RPS/concurrency assumptions behind the 8->20 sizing.

My rough sizing rationale: we estimated ~120 concurrent tokens-generating streams at peak for the pilot and ~350 concurrent streams under burst (clients are short prompts, average 40 tokens generation), which maps to the autoscale to 20 A100-equivalents for sub-200ms per-token SLO in our benchmark. But I want ops to validate if continuous batching and cache-warmup will be sufficient or if we should recommend a larger base pool.

Specific operational confirmations needed: 
- Can we enable log forwarder to Aster's Splunk (platform@asterhealth.com) with 180-day retention?
- What exact autoscale thresholds should we set (util% and queued requests) to avoid oscillation during bursts?
- Warmup plan: can we run a k=100 prefix warmup job 120 minutes prior to window? Any objections to running that job automatically?

Also tagging in the SOW and activation-checklist attachments (attached). If you prefer, I can open INF ticket and schedule a short triage call with Aster's infra.

Thanks,
Priyom
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: AsterHealth dedicated pool activation — sprint & regional priority agreement

Thanks for the context — quick ops answers below (cc: I've added key infra folks to the Jira INF-4523 ticket for tracking).

1) Logs / retention / Splunk: We can stream audit & request logs to customer Splunk via secure forwarder. Retention is a customer-side setting; we will retain our internal copies for 365 days by default. From a contract perspective we can state 180 days of retention in the SOW. See attachment: pool-config-template.json (sample config).

2) Sizing and concurrency assumptions: Your concurrent-stream numbers sound reasonable. Our internal perf data maps ~16 streams per A100-equivalent for 40-token average generation at your SLO. That gives ~8 GPUs * 16 = 128 concurrent streams baseline; burst to 20 -> 320 concurrent streams. We'll recommend the 8->20 plan but add a safety cushion: increase base to 10 if Aster expects heavier initial parallelism or longer responses.

3) Autoscale thresholds: Propose: scale-up when 65% sustained GPU utilization OR queued-request depth > 150 for a 45s window; scale-down when sustained utilization < 40% for 5m and queue < 40. These thresholds reduce oscillation while respecting latency targets.

4) Warmup job: Yes — we can run a KV/prefix warmup targeting k=100, 2 hours before the scheduled window. We'll execute the warmup via the ops-runbook and report results to the triage loop.

5) Preflight window: We can reserve a 4-hour preflight on 2027-05-18 08:00–12:00 PT (us-west1). Ops SLA: we'll have on-call infra and real-time metrics dashboards during the window.

Attachments: pool-config-template.json (sample), link to INF-4523.

If Priyom / Monica approve, I'll post these numbers to the SOW and propose a signed activation date of 2027-05-20 for limited go-live, expanding after a 3-day validation period.

—Karthik
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@asterhealth.com>, Platform Team <platform@asterhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AsterHealth dedicated pool activation — sprint & regional priority agreement

Elaine — thanks for the quick turnaround, and Karthik thanks for the clear ops commitments. To summarize (actionable items):

- Regions: us-west1 primary; us-east1 secondary (confirmed).
- Capacity: start with 8 GPUs reserved; ops recommends bumping to 10 if Aster expects higher parallelism. For now, we'll proceed with 8->20 burst plan and track utilization closely during preflight.
- Autoscale: use Karthik's thresholds (scale-up: 65% or queued>150 for 45s; scale-down: <40% for 5m and queued<40).
- Warmup: KV/prefix k=100, run 2 hours before each scheduled window.
- Logs: Redwood will stream audit & request logs to Aster Splunk; SOW will state 180-day retention and ops will maintain internal 365-day copy.
- Preflight: reserved 2027-05-18 08:00–12:00 PT; target limited go-live 2027-05-20.

Next steps: 
1) Elaine / AsterHealth — please confirm acceptance of the above and sign the attached SOW v2 (DocuSign link included).
2) Monica / Ops — please update INF-4523 with the final pool-config and add the preflight checklist from activation-checklist.csv.
3) I'll schedule a 30-minute preflight kickoff with Aster and infra for 2027-05-17 to walk the warmup and roll-back plan.

If no objections I'll move forward with the SOW and calendar invites.

Best,
Priyom
